findings.motion: Do pass, Assembly Local Government Committee
findings.note: Voted in favour in the Assembly Local Government Committee on SB 1174, which bars local governments from requiring ID to vote (committee vote 7 to 2).

findings.passage: Yeah, absolutely. Consistency across our state in how we process elections I think is key to the confidence that we have in our elections. So thank you for doing this bill. Happy to support.
findings.note: Said in committee on SB 1174, the bill barring local voter-ID rules, as transcribed by Digital Democracy.
Voted in favour on the Assembly floor of SB 1174; the roll lists him among the ayes.

findings.passage: And if this as a moment, to be able to maybe exchange some dialogue and set the record straight, you know, the history that we have in this country around ID requirements is both racist and discriminatory and really has been able to interfere with an individual Americans right to be able to exercise their right to vote.
findings.note: Floor speech in support of SB 1174, as transcribed by Digital Democracy.

findings.passage: Now, there is no evidence of non citizens voting in our elections. This is something that is maliciously spread across social media and taken as fact.
findings.note: Same floor speech; speaks on non-citizen voting claims.

findings.passage: It compromises our ability to be able to have faith in our mail-in voting system because of course that is something that is signed for on the back of your envelope and have to be matched back at your registrar of voters. No ID required.
findings.note: Same floor speech; describes how mail ballots are checked by signature, with no ID required.

findings.passage: We have faith in our Secretary of State and we have faith in our elections process here in the state of California. And it is the root of that faith that compels us to stay the course and make sure that we are not changing our standards when it comes to voter ID.
findings.note: Same floor speech; on keeping California's current voter-ID standard.
